selection.rationale: Objective wiring: generated_tokens_per_second for the frozen offline workload is batch 8 x 32 fixed greedy tokens over the end-to-end wall; single device, communication not applicable per resources.json. Independently measured original baseline (project.json): 831.169 ms end-to-end = 124.783 ms prefill + 706.391 ms decode = 307.9999 tok/s, so decode is about 85 percent of the wall and the only phase with large editable headroom, while prefill is busy-bound (131.2 ms hooked busy vs 124.8 ms wall). Concrete failure being repaired (inputs/previous-feedback.txt, trial-6002d1ef9b, decision no_valid_parameter_candidate, n_complete=0 n_fail=1, with audit): four decode/root CUDA-graph attempts (7ee056ddc4, eeb66b190e, 82eb37adf6, 6002d1ef9b) all failed quality with the byte-identical deterministic signature 10,431,056 / 38,895,616 mismatched logits elements (26.8 percent), max abs 4.0, and the latest additionally failed exact token identity at step 0. Code-level fact from the actual previous implementation (inputs/previous-candidate/candidate.py, replacement(): the capture branch _capture(step) falls straight through to reading st["hidden"][step] and running lm_head on it): torch.cuda.graph capture records work without executing it, so on every capture invocation - all 31 steps of the first run - the returned logits were computed from uninitialized private-pool memory. That is a direct computation/state error matching the new step-0 token failure. Combined with the audit observation that an unconditional output clone (82eb37adf6) and an eagerly allocated lm_head output (6002d1ef9b) both left the 26.8 percent signature untouched, output aliasing is not established as the cause; the surviving explanation is that the captured kernel sequence itself diverges deterministically from eager numerics (capture-time backend/algorithm selection plus the shared-pool KV cat chain), which no output-ownership change can cure. Per the audit the hypothesis is changed rather than retried: this selection removes stream capture entirely and keeps every kernel eager. Selected boundary: region scope anchored on group c87ceac9604a34476cf4 (decode-phase transformers.models.qwen3.modeling_qwen3.Qwen3ForCausalLM module; single call 323bcbe006b343648b346af9, 31 invocations, kwargs input_ids [8,1] int64 cuda / past_key_values DynamicCache / use_cache True / logits_to_keep 1, hooked diagnostic 447.466 ms). Verified against calls.json: the 23,261 ids in affected_calls are exactly the complete set of decode-phase calls in the trace (22,715 functional + 546 module) - every observed call nested inside the region (Qwen3Model, 36 Qwen3DecoderLayer per step, Linear/aten::linear projections, Qwen3MLP, Qwen3Attention, scaled_dot_product_attention, RMSNorm mean/pow/rsqrt/mul chains, rotary mul/neg/cat, DynamicCache cat appends, dtype casts) re-executes under the replacement; the 112 profiler bookkeeping calls and 7 loop-level adapter calls (argmax/unsqueeze/to/expand/select) execute outside the model call and stay unchanged. Replacement mechanism, eager and capture-free with kernel-for-kernel identity: (1) Per-run preallocated KV workspace - step 0 binds the run fresh eager prefill K/V by device copies into a persistent per-layer [batch, kv_heads, 288, head_dim] workspace (about 330 MB bf16); each step writes its one-token k/v in place (narrow-slice copy_) and SDPA consumes the contiguous prefix slice, which holds byte-identical values to what DynamicCache.update torch.cat would have produced. This deletes the decode aten::cat family (2,306 hooked calls, 20.905 ms hooked busy; every step rewrites the whole growing cache across 36 layers x K+V), the per-step allocation churn and the DynamicCache bookkeeping, without changing any kernel input value. (2) Flattened eager step executor - the identical aten op sequence (same aten::linear calls on the same parameter tensors, same SDPA signature, same RMSNorm/rotary chains on identically-valued tensors) is invoked with pre-resolved module parameters, bypassing nn.Module dispatch, hook checks and per-layer cache-object construction. Same shapes reach cublas and SDPA, so algorithm selection and results are bit-identical to the pristine parent - the safety property capture could not guarantee here and eager retains. (3) output.logits is produced by the parent logits_to_keep=1 path (lm_head on the last-position hidden state) as a freshly allocated eager tensor every invocation; nothing ever rewrites it, so the adapter detached views (adapter.py lines 152/168) cannot alias. output.past_key_values is a genuine DynamicCache over the workspace slices at the run current length, consumed unchanged by the frozen loop and by any parent fallback. (4) Guards: exact kwargs set, input_ids [8,1] int64 cuda, use_cache True, logits_to_keep 1, exact DynamicCache type, uniform layer geometry, batch/dtype consistency; any mismatch calls the pristine parent with the original arguments. No capture, no private pools, no latches; nothing survives across runs except the workspace, fully re-bound from each run own prefill at step 0. Prefill stays eager and untouched; timing boundaries, argmax and workload semantics are the source own. Not selected: prefill region (busy-bound, 15 percent share); GEMM provider/operator replacement (fixed provider, and the 26.8 percent signature shows the 0.02 logits gate with exact greedy tokens effectively demands near-bit-identical numerics, which also excludes torch.compile, custom fused kernels and batched/fused GEMM restructures in this step); speculative or multi-token decode (the frozen completion contract is exactly 31 subsequent one-token forwards); communication (single device). All CUDA microseconds quoted are hooked discovery diagnostics on a run whose profiled wall was 11,965 ms against the 831 ms clean wall - bounds only, never wall claims.
selection.hypothesis: Quality gates (hard, both paired repeats): exact greedy token equality and stacked last-position logits within atol=rtol=0.02 with effectively zero mismatching elements; the replacement is bit-identical by construction (same eager kernels, same shapes, same values), verified during development by torch.equal of per-step returned logits and per-step K/V workspace slices against a pristine eager parent before and after the step-0 bind. Recurrence of the 26.8-percent / max-abs-4.0 mismatch signature, or any token mismatch including step 0, rejects the candidate outright - no further capture-based retries. Coverage: 62/62 engagements of call 323bcbe006b343648b346af9 with zero parent fallbacks and math_policy_unchanged=true. Performance (falsifiable prediction, tested only by the framework clean paired repeats, not a guarantee): removing per-step cat copy traffic and launches (about 74 hooked cat calls per step), per-step allocation churn, DynamicCache and module-dispatch overhead recovers part of the decode idle bounded by the hooked diagnostics (706.391 ms clean decode wall vs 447.466 ms hooked region busy, about 259 ms or 8.35 ms per step across 31 steps); decode wall is expected to fall to roughly 590-650 ms and end-to-end from 831.2 ms to roughly 715-775 ms, raising generated_tokens_per_second from 308.0 to about 330-358 tok/s (+7-16 percent). Acceptance requires a strictly positive measured gain with all quality gates green; a measured null result with green gates is reported as such and the candidate is not accepted on predicted benefit alone. The fallback path is performance-neutral (pristine parent). Memory: the persistent workspace adds about 330 MB to peak allocated bytes (baseline peak 8.65 GB, reserved 8.86 GB), reported as measured allocator counters.

proposal.rationale: Repair of the concrete failure in inputs/previous-feedback.txt (trial-6002d1ef9b, decision no_valid_parameter_candidate, n_complete=0 n_fail=1) and of the three same-signature graph attempts before it (7ee056ddc4, eeb66b190e, 82eb37adf6): every decode/root CUDA-graph bundle failed quality with the byte-identical signature 10,431,056 / 38,895,616 mismatched logits elements (26.8%, max abs 4.0), and the latest additionally failed exact greedy-token identity on the capture run. Reading the actual prior implementation shows the computation/state error directly: torch.cuda.graph stream capture records work without executing it, so on all 31 capture invocations the post-capture eager lm_head read uninitialized private-pool memory (hence wrong step-0 tokens), while on replay runs the captured kernel sequence diverged deterministically from eager numerics (capture-time backend/algorithm selection plus the pool-resident KV cat chain). Because trial-82eb37adf6 already cloned its output buffer unconditionally and trial-6002d1ef9b already produced logits eagerly outside the graphs without curing the 26.8% signature, output ownership is ruled out as the cause; per the audit the hypothesis is changed rather than retried: this candidate contains no stream capture, no graph pools and no static-cache wrapper anywhere. Replacement mechanism (call 323bcbe006b343648b346af9, decode-phase Qwen3ForCausalLM.forward, 31 invocations per run, kwargs input_ids [8,1] int64 / past_key_values DynamicCache / use_cache True / logits_to_keep 1): a flattened eager executor that dispatches the identical aten op sequence as the pristine parent - embedding lookup; per layer input RMSNorm (fp32 upcast, pow(2), mean, add-eps, rsqrt, mul, downcast, weight-mul), q/k/v linear + view, q/k RMSNorm, transpose, rotary chains (slice/neg/cat/mul/add on unsqueezed cos/sin), KV append, scaled_dot_product_attention with the exact parent signature (attn_mask None, dropout_p 0.0, scale=head_dim**-0.5, is_causal False, enable_gqa True), o_proj, residual adds, post RMSNorm, gate/up/silu/mul/down MLP; final RMSNorm; lm_head on [:, -1:, :] - on the same parameter tensors with the same shapes, dtypes, strides classes and values, so the same eager kernels run kernel-for-kernel. Two structural changes remove host and memory traffic without touching any kernel input value: (1) a persistent per-layer [8, 8, 288, 128] bf16 KV workspace (36 layers x K+V) into which step 0 of every run binds the run's fresh eager prefill K/V by 72 device copies; each step then writes its one-token k/v in place (narrow-slice copy_) and hands SDPA the prefix slice, byte-identical to what DynamicCache.update torch.cat would have produced - deleting the 72 whole-cache cat rewrites per step (2,306 hooked decode cats, 20.9 ms hooked busy; about 4.9 GB of read+write cat traffic per run at kv lengths 257..287), their allocation churn and the DynamicCache Python bookkeeping; (2) a RoPE cos/sin table for positions 256..295 built once from the live inv_freq buffer with the parent's exact op sequence (fp32 outer-product matmul, cat, cos, sin, scaling mul, bf16 cast); every element is a scalar-only product/cast with no reduction-order freedom, so per-step slices are byte-identical to the parent's per-step tensors (verified), while the per-step rotary/arange/mask module machinery disappears. The returned past_key_values remains the incoming DynamicCache object with layer tensors re-pointed to workspace prefix views only after a step fully succeeds, so a mid-run parent fallback consumes a fully valid cache; guard failures fall back per-call and poison the remainder of the run, unexpected exceptions latch permanently, and coverage would show any fallback. The adapter-visible ABI, tokens, logits capture and state semantics are unchanged; prefill is not replaced (different call id) and runs pristine. Evidence gathered before submission on the worker interpreter (transformers 5.16.1, torch 2.13.0+cu129, CPU-only, no device lease): with tiny and production-geometry Qwen3 models (32 q heads / 8 kv heads / head_dim 128 / hidden 2560, bf16 and fp32, prefill 256, 31 decode steps, batch 8), the replacement's stacked per-step logits, tokens and final K/V caches are torch.equal to the pristine parent across multiple runs, geometry re-binds, forced mid-run guard fallbacks (outputs stay exact, route latches to parent for the run) and fresh-run recovery; F.embedding was fixed to pass max_norm/norm_type by keyword after an initial positional-argument bug was caught by exactly this harness. On-GPU validation remains the framework's paired repeats. Falsifiable performance expectation (prediction, not a guarantee): the removed cost is host dispatch and cat traffic only - about 36 layer-module dispatch stacks, ~10 nn.Module __call__s per layer, DynamicCache.update and rotary/mask Python per step (~4-6 ms/step of the ~8.35 ms/step host overhead implied by 706.4 ms clean decode wall vs 447.5 ms hooked region busy), plus ~0.14 ms/step of cat device traffic and per-step allocator churn. Decode wall is expected to fall from 706.4 ms to roughly 590-650 ms and end-to-end from 831.2 ms to roughly 715-775 ms, raising generated_tokens_per_second from 308.0 to about 330-358 tok/s (+7-16%); the device floor (weight-read bound GEMMs at batch 8 x 1 token) is untouched. A measured null result with green gates is reported as null; recurrence of the 26.8% / max-abs-4.0 signature or any token mismatch rejects outright.

setup_work.when: build() performs attribute capture and structure validation only (no CUDA work at import or build time). The workspace and rope table are allocated on the first decode invocation - inside the warmup phase, outside timed measure runs - and persist for the process lifetime; every subsequent run rebinds with device copies before its first decode step.
steps: build(): validate model structure (no sliding layers, rope_type default, bias-free attention projections, uniform weight geometry across the 36 layers, kv head groups > 1) and prebind per-layer tuples (norm weights/eps, q/k/v/o/gate/up/down weights, sdpa scale), embedding/lm_head/final-norm parameters and the live rotary inv_freq buffer.

first invocation (warmup): allocate 72 persistent bf16 workspaces [8, 8, 288, 128] (339,738,624 bytes) outside inference mode; build the [1, 40, 128] bf16 cos/sin table for positions base_len..base_len+39 (20,480 bytes) with the parent's exact op sequence.

per run (step 0 of decode): bind - 72 narrow-slice copy_ of the run's fresh eager prefill K/V into workspace slots [0:256] (301,989,888 bytes copied, sub-millisecond device time, amortized over 31 steps).

per timed decode step: one F.embedding, per layer 8-op RMSNorms (x2), q/k/v/o+gate/up/down linears, rope chains, two 1-token slot copy_, one SDPA on prefix views, MLP, residuals (about 1,850 kernels/step, same kernel classes as parent); after the layer loop, re-point the 36 cache layers to prefix views and run lm_head on [:, -1:, :]. Everything is issued on the current (default) stream like the parent's ops; no extra device synchronization is introduced inside the workload boundary.

setup_allocation_bytes.notes: The workspace is allocated once (first warmup invocation) and retained across runs; it is reused, not reallocated, when the frozen geometry repeats. Geometry changes (never in the frozen workload) would reallocate.

setup_work.memory_reporting: framework.peak_allocated_bytes per run rises by the persistent 339.7 MB workspace after the first allocation (baseline peak 8,651,642,880 -> about 8.99e9) and framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated_bytes / lifecycle_peak_reserved_bytes include this setup allocation plus the per-run bind copies; reserved grows by roughly the same amount. These are allocator-counter observations, not a claim of physical-memory savings; no non-PyTorch driver allocation and no CUDA Graph pool is involved. The removed cat churn slightly lowers transient allocator turnover inside runs.

quality_risks: Bit-exactness: every dispatched op mirrors the parent's aten call on identically-valued tensors (verified torch.equal on logits/tokens/KV for tiny and production-geometry models on the worker interpreter, CPU). The one deliberate input-layout difference is that SDPA consumes prefix slices of the persistent workspace (head/seq strides of a 288-slot buffer) instead of freshly cat-ed contiguous tensors; the values are byte-identical, last-dim strides and 16-byte pointer alignment are preserved, so flash/efficient eligibility and selection are unchanged, and the kernels are deterministic - but GPU backend selection cannot be observed from the agent shell, so this remains the residual numerical risk, falsifiable by the framework's paired logits gate.

cuBLAS heuristics key on shapes/strides/dtypes and alignment buckets; the replacement allocates the same size classes as the parent's eager path (512-byte-aligned allocator blocks) and uses the same parameter tensors, so algorithm selection is expected to match. The captured-kernel-divergence mechanism of the four failed graph attempts cannot recur here because no capture exists.

Guard deviations (kwargs set, input_ids shape/dtype, use_cache/logits_to_keep flags, cache type/layer count/geometry/dtype, module training, step range) fall back per-call to the pristine parent with the original arguments and poison the remainder of the run; unexpected exceptions latch permanently to the parent. Fallbacks appear in coverage counts and reject the candidate rather than silently changing semantics.

Mid-run state safety: cache layer tensors are re-pointed to workspace prefix views only after the full step succeeds, so a mid-step exception leaves the incoming cache exactly as the parent left it and the parent fallback (or a poisoned-run parent continuation) consumes a valid DynamicCache; cross-run contamination is impossible because every run rebinds slots [0:256] from its own fresh prefill before any fast step.

Workspace capacity is base_len+32 slots and the rope table covers 40 decode steps; the frozen workload needs 31. A longer hypothetical sequence degrades to pristine-parent fallback (correct, coverage-visible), never to wrong values.

Quality-mode logits are fresh eager tensors from the final linear, so adapter-held detached views cannot be rewritten by later steps (no pool memory is involved); tokens are produced by the unchanged adapter argmax on the returned logits.

The replacement runs under the adapter's torch.inference_mode() context exactly like the parent; the workspace/table are allocated under torch.inference_mode(False) so in-place updates remain legal in every later context.
